QF.id: AIFM Fee Structure and Fund Performance_24

question.text: The DPI (Distributions to Paid-In) multiple of a Category II AIF is BEST interpreted as:

answer.text: A realisation multiple — the cash already returned to investors divided by capital paid in
A measure of unrealised fund value
The NAV per unit at fund inception
A measure of the fund's leverage

explanation.text: The Logic: DPI = Total Distributions / Total Capital Contributions (Paid-In Capital). It is the realisation multiple and tells LPs how much cash has been returned per rupee contributed. The Trap: Option B describes RVPI (residual value). Option C is an NAV concept. Option D confuses DPI with leverage. Note: The DPI definition is set out in the fund performance chapter of the workbook.
